sentences.text:
This Petition Coming On For Admission This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Accused Nos.1 to 15 are before this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C with a prayer to quash the order dated 09.05.2023 passed by the Court of the Civil Judge and JMFC, Jewargi, Kalaburagi District taking cognizance by issuing process to the said accused in C.C.No.342/2023 (arising out of Crime No.109/2022 registered by the Nelogi Police Station, Kalaburagi District) for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 323, 324, 355, 504 and 506 read with Section 149 of IPC.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3824 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondents.

3. FIR in Crime No.109/2022 was registered by the Nelogi Police Station, Kalaburagi against the petitioners herein and four others for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 21.08.2022 received from respondent No.2 herein.
The police after investigation have filed charge-sheet in the said case against 15 persons.
The petitioners are arrayed as accused No.1 to 15 in the charge-sheet.

The Trial Court by the order impugned has taken cognizance of the charge-sheeted offences and directed the Registry to register criminal case against the accused for the charge- sheeted offences and has issued summons to the accused.
Being aggrieved by the same, accused No.1 to 15 are before this Court.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that daughter of accused Nos.1 and 2 is married NC: 2024:KHC-K:3824 to respondent No.2.
There is a dispute between respondent No.2 and his wife.

The wife of respondent No.2 has filed a criminal case against respondent No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323,
504 and 506 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

In the said case, the police Laxmanrao And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181232567/
4 after investigation have filed charge-sheet and criminal case is now pending against respondent No.2 in C.C.No.26950/2022 before the Court of ACJM, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: He submits that only as a counter to the said case, a false complaint has been lodged without any basis against the petitioners herein.

He submits that registration of the case against the petitioners and continuation of the further proceedings which is impugned in this petition would amount to abuse of process of law and accordingly, prays to allow the petition.
5.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1/State and counsel for respondent No.2 have opposed the petition.

They submit NC: 2024:KHC-K:3824 that FIR was registered against respondent No.2 herein in Crime No.188/2022 by the Whitefield Police Station,
Bengaluru City for the offences punishable under Sections 506, 34, 498A and 504 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act on the basis of the first information received from Smt.Ashwini, who is his wife and after investigation charge-sheet is filed in the said case and respondent No.2 is being tried for the charge-sheeted offences in Crime No.188/2022 before the jurisdictional Court in C.C.No.26950/2022.
They submit that the incident in question has nothing to do with the said case which is registered against respondent No.2.
Petitioners have committed the offence on 13.08.2022 and in the said incident, respondent No.2 has suffered injury.

6. It is averred in the first information which has resulted in registering FIR in Crime No.109/2022 against the petitioners herein that the accused persons were threatening the first informant after his wife had lodged a criminal case against him.

On 13.08.2022 the petitioners NC: 2024:KHC-K:3824 came to the house of respondent No.2 in vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-32-P-8809 and two other vehicles on the guise of holding a nyayapanchayat and started abusing him.

When the mother of first informant questioned the act of accused, accused No.14 and 15 allegedly abused her using filthy language and when this was objected to by the respondent No.2 first informant even he was abused by the accused persons using filthy language.

Thereafter, accused Nos.14 and 15 started assaulting the first informant and when the brother of first informant tried to interfere, accused No.11 and accused No.9 assaulted him with their hands on his cheek and kicked him.
When the first informant's sister Nagamma arrived to the spot of crime, accused No.2 allegedly caught hold of her hair and started pulling her and assaulting her on her stomach with his hands.

It is alleged that the other accused persons were present at the spot of crime also abused and assaulted the first informant and his relatives and only after the villagers intervened, the accused persons threatened the first informant and his family members NC: 2024:KHC-K:3824 with dire consequences to their life and thereafter left the place.
The police after investigation have filed charge- sheet as against petitioners herein who are arrayed as accused No.1 to 15.
The police have recorded statement of 14 witnesses during the course of investigation, who are cited as charge-sheet witnesses 1 to 14.

CW.1 is the injured who is the first informant in the present case, CW.2 and CW.3 are the panchas to the spot mahazar, CW.4 to CW.12 are the eyewitnesses to the incident in question and the other witnesses are the Investigating Officers in the present case.
7. In the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C of the first informant and the eyewitnesses recorded by the Investigating Officer specific allegations are found as against the accused persons herein.
It is only based on such statements made by the charge-sheet witnesses the petitioners herein are arrayed as accused Nos.1 to 15 in the charge-sheet.

Therefore, it cannot be said that there is Laxmanrao And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181232567/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: absolutely no material in the charge-sheet to prosecute - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3824 the petitioners for the alleged offence.

The inherent power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C can be exercised to quash the criminal proceedings, if only it is found that charge-sheet is filed against the accused not supported with any material and the allegations made in the charge-sheet against the accused are totally baseless.

In the case on hand, the statements of the first informant and the eyewitnesses who are cited as charge-sheet witnesses has been recorded and the same would prima facie show the involvement of petitioners herein in the alleged incident that had taken place on 13.08.2022.

Merely for the reason that a criminal case has been registered against respondent No.2 on the basis of the complaint filed by the daughter of petitioner Nos.1 and 2 herein, the same cannot be a ground for quashing the present criminal proceedings when the material on record would prima facie show that the police during the course of investigation have collected sufficient material to prosecute the petitioners to the charge-sheeted offences.
Under the circumstances, I do not find any good reason to entertain this petition.
Accordingly, the following ORDER The criminal petition is dismissed.
